pcb.scope: Native board geometry; nominal PDF tolerance difference preserved.

cover.scope: Native component also includes folded flex; complete component depth is not front glass thickness.

screen.basis: PDF active area and native LCD component1 face32 agree. Framebuffer is projected through the cover onto the native viewing face component0 face11 at0.65 mm, plus0.008 mm rendering offset; outer cover rim remains0.70 mm.

inspectionGroups.notes: Debugging separation of complete native optical components, including their folded flex; not an assembly instruction or reconstructed operating spacing.

limitations: All 728 native source components, including five open shells, are retained in their original millimetre assembly positions. Small components are grouped for rendering only; each source index is independently exported and bounds-checked.

SKU35065 includes a separate lithium battery; SKU35066 (-EN) omits it. This model is the native board/display assembly, without an invented battery or external speaker placement. No additional enclosure is present in the supplied assembly.

The 0.70 mm cover reference in the PDF is a front laminate dimension. Native touch component0 also includes folded flex reaching below the PCB; its 7.00 mm total component depth is not glass thickness.
The LCD AA is 43.20×57.60 mm. The separate touch VA is 43.80×58.20 mm, and cover outer size50.54×73.06 mm has R2 corners. The runtime uses rectangular AA, not cover or VA dimensions.
Native PCB49.913581×69.011087×1.600000 mm differs slightly from PDF nominal49.90×69.00×1.60 mm. Native geometry is preserved without scaling.

BOOT is physical component9 and binds to runtime control boot, GPIO9 active-low. RESET component8 and power component712 remain visible but unbound; PWR belongs to the CH32/power circuit and is not exposed as a fictitious ordinary GPIO key.

Native shielding part271 has the reused library name ESP32-WROOM-32E_SHIELDING_CASE_. This is a mechanical library label in the published C6 assembly; it is not evidence that the board uses a classic ESP32. The actual C6 module identity comes from separate electrical sources and photographs.

Native colors are retained except for a dark optical cover and black PCB, selected from the exact official photographs. Source photographs remain unchanged references and no stock screenshot replaces the live framebuffer.

Optical text-to-USB registration and physical fit have not been calibrated on hardware. The identity transform preserves the supplied portrait assembly and 240×320 framebuffer shape; firmware/native execution is separately documented.
Repository and CAD dates are source dates, not a product release-date certification or proof of a specific shipping PCB revision.
Native parts are not Boolean-unioned; any source assembly overlaps remain as provided. The 0.008 mm screen offset is a rendering offset, not a physical layer.
No pre-reset model, source archive or lost historical acceptance result is reused.

The independently downloaded exact C6 STEP is linewise identical to the preceding C5 mechanical export; only line endings differ. This does not equate their chips, GPIO routes or firmware. C6 board-specific source and simulation are recorded separately.

sourceSearch.result: Exact C6 source STEP and mechanical PDF downloaded from the pinned official tree. All 728 native components retain their original millimetre coordinates. Canonical resource links use an older directory layout.
